headline: Smoke Smell After a Fire: Myths vs. Facts
articleBody: When a fire impacts your home, the lingering smoke smell can be really tough to deal with, and there are lots of misconceptions out there. Let's clear some up. Myth: Airing out your home for a few days will make the smoke smell disappear completely. Fact: While ventilation helps, smoke particles embed themselves deeply into porous materials like drywall, carpets, and upholstery. Simply airing it out won't remove these trapped odors; professional cleaning is often needed for full remediation. Myth: All smoke smells are the same. Fact: Not true! The type of smoke (e.g., from wood, synthetic materials, or protein fires) impacts how intense the odor is and how difficult it is to remove. Synthetic materials, for instance, often produce a much more pungent and sticky residue. Myth: You can just paint over the smell. Fact: Painting over smoke-damaged walls without proper cleaning and sealing is a temporary fix at best. The odor will eventually bleed through the paint. Proper cleaning, sealing with an odor-blocking primer, and then painting is the right approach. Myth: If you can't see soot, there's no smoke damage. Fact: Invisible smoke particles can still permeate your home, impacting air quality and leaving an odor, even without visible soot. Getting rid of smoke smell completely takes more than just a quick clean. When in doubt, call First To Respond Restoration for expert help.
